text: Claude has 240 days to turn timber into profit. First, it has to cross this river.
Plan: one straight timber road along row 68, a short bridge over the river, and a shared depot by the sawmill. Wood first, goods second.
First capital commitment: roads, bridge and stops cost about 13,700. Now two 20-tonne wood trucks; I'll add more only if wood piles up at the forest.
Both wood trucks are rolling west over the bridge to wait for full loads at the forest.
Correction: after 30 days the trucks never reached the forest. I suspect my separately built road pieces don't join up, so I'm explicitly linking the junctions and entrances.
Both trucks are at the forest stop. The trip took about 25 days, so I'm checking how fast the forest fills them before buying anything else.
Bottleneck: the forest gives roughly 2.4 tonnes a day, but a round trip takes about 50 days. Two trucks would only reach 120 tonnes near the deadline, so I'm adding a third wood truck.
First wood delivery: 20 tonnes unloaded at the sawmill stop. Now I'm watching for goods output and income.
Wood pays about 470 per load. I'm buying a single goods truck now so the sawmill stop gets a goods rating. Two 14-crate loads cover the target, and one truck keeps costs low.
First goods: the sawmill has loaded 13 crates into the goods truck. The forest stop holds 22 tonnes waiting, so three wood trucks are enough. No more buying.
14 crates delivered to Eastmere, which is halfway to the goods target. Cash is back above 8,000 and the wood trucks keep feeding the mill.
Wood target verified: 120 tonnes delivered to the sawmill. The goods truck is on its second run with 14 crates, so the whole result now depends on that trip.

Verified result on day 199: 140 tonnes of wood reached the sawmill and 28 crates of goods reached Eastmere. I finished with 9,533 cash, 3,307 truck operating profit, four trucks and no extra borrowing. All targets met.
Thanks for watching The Agent Terrarium. See you next time.
